issues.description: nevra[0] indexes the first character of the filename, not the first letter of the package name
issues.detail: Koji's canonical path uses the first letter of the package NAME (e.g. 'k' for kernel-...), but `nevra[0]` takes the first character of the full filename string. For NEVRAs starting with a digit (e.g. '389-ds-base-...') or other non-alpha prefix, this produces a wrong directory and a 404. Should parse the package name and lowercase its first letter.

issues.description: extract_arch_from_url can return None and silently produce a malformed URL
issues.detail: If the arch regex finds no match (e.g. an unexpected URL shape, or a noarch package), `extract_arch_from_url` returns None and the f-string becomes '.../latest/None/Packages/...'. The function should raise or skip with a clear error rather than emit a broken URL that only fails at fetch time in CI.

issues.description: noarch packages are rewritten under an arch-specific Packages directory
issues.detail: noarch RPMs in Koji live under `latest/<arch>/Packages/...` only for the arch tree they were tagged into; the rewrite blindly uses whatever arch the regex finds in the source URL. If a noarch RPM URL came from a path lacking a recognized arch token, the result is either None or a wrong directory. Worth explicitly handling noarch.

issues.description: Substring check `koji_url_base in url` is brittle if hostnames change
issues.detail: Detection of an existing coreos-pool URL relies on a substring match against one hardcoded hostname. A future mirror, alternate host, or staging URL containing coreos-pool elsewhere in the path would not be rewritten or could be misclassified. Consider parsing the URL and matching host+path prefix explicitly.

issues.description: Word-boundary regex relies on ordering of alternatives
issues.detail: The arches list order matters because regex alternation is left-to-right and `aarch64` contains `arch`. The current list is fine, but if someone later adds e.g. 'arm' or reorders, partial matches could occur. A small comment or sorting by length descending would harden this.

issues.description: Race condition and untestable lockfile changes acknowledged but not mitigated
issues.detail: The PR description notes a race between bump-lockfile merge and coreos-koji-tagger, plus inability to test rpms.lock.yaml locally. No retry, verification, or HEAD-check is added against the crafted URL. At minimum a follow-up issue or a TODO in code would help future maintainers understand the known gap.

review.summary: The patch cleanly centralizes URL rewriting to coreos-pool, but the canonical Koji path construction has a real bug: `nevra[0]` takes the first character of the filename rather than the first letter of the package name, which produces wrong directories for any NEVRA whose filename doesn't start with the package's first letter (digits, etc.). Error handling is also weak — `extract_arch_from_url` returning None leads to a literal 'None' in the URL rather than a fail-fast error, and noarch packages aren't explicitly considered. The known race/testability gaps in the PR description are accepted but not mitigated in code. Worth fixing before merge.
